label: early original-phase inputs r/o/s/t/3/x/p/z/f (strongest on r)
explanation: Fires only during the original (input) phase, essentially never at t=0, at the delimiter, or during copy. Most activation is at positions 1-3 and it drops off sharply after position 4. The input token gates it: r is by far the strongest (35% of activation mass, 9x lift), then o, s, t, 3, x, p, z, f; almost no other token ever fires it. It is mostly on the first occurrence of the token (90% of mass). The necessary condition (one of those tokens at t=1..4) covers about 96% of activations and 97% of mass, but only about 11% of such steps fire, so precision is low. Whether it fires depends on earlier context: it fires more when the sequence starts with e/k/h/b/y/v/u/r (adding that condition gives F1 about 0.31, precision about 0.22), and the strongest examples are r after k/e/y-type prefixes. I could not find a simple predicate that pins down which context it needs.
